card.title: 334th MOUNTAIN RIFLES
card.flavorText: The 334th Rifle Regiment was a unit of the 47th Mountain Rifle Division of the Red Army during WWII. On 24 September 1941 the division was sent to participate in an attack on Poltava which had been occupied by the Germans a few days earlier. However, the Soviet forces were forced into a disorganized retreat from the area, where the 47th Division lost 23 artillery guns and 7 mortars. In May 1942, as part of the 6th Army, the division fought in the Second Battle of Kharkov, which resulted in an Axis victory, and where the 47th Mountain Rifle Division was wiped out. The division was reformed in July 1942, and in 1943 it fought in the Nevel Offensive as part of the 83rd Rifle Corps. Afterwards the 47th Division was awarded the honorific title “Nevel” for its part in capturing the town. The division was later awarded the Order of Suvorov and the Order of Lenin for its actions. It was disbanded after the war.
